opti-1: Pensacola Beach, Florida. It looks like snow, but it's soft white sand.
opti-2: Then, on January 21, 2025, real snow fell in Florida!
opti-4: High in freezing clouds, water turned into snow. Fields turned white.
opti-5: That night, the air stayed below freezing.
opti-7: Sunlight warmed the snow, and it melted into water.
opti-8: Soon even the puddles were gone. Where did the water go?
opti-9: What happens to matter when it gets hotter or colder?
27-01-welcome: Our film starts on a snowy day in Florida. First, inspect a tiny frozen mystery from long ago.
27-01-lesson: Today you're a matter scientist. Follow an ice cube, test heat and cold, then climb down a sky ladder.
27-01-check: Three quick questions. It's not graded. It's just for you, so give each one your best try.
27-01-assign: Time to show what you learned. Name each change, then draw water's whole cycle.
how-27-01-specimen: Press Inspect specimen. Move the magnifying lens over the star, then tap 3 things you notice.
how-27-01-compare: Put the sun lamp under one tray and the freezer pack under the other: drag them, or tap one, then a tray. Press Run the test. Then swap.
how-27-01-wall: First, make a prediction. Then brush the glowing step: drag across it (or tap it again and again) until the photo shows.
how-27-01-det: Pick three files, one at a time. Tap a clue, then name the change. Predict if heat was added or taken away, and watch the place appear.
how-27-01-partc: Draw the full state-change cycle for water. Show solid, liquid, and gas with arrows between them. Label each arrow: melting, freezing, evaporation, or condensation. Use color to show hot and cold.
